stem:
Parth fills the three cells in the figure with the numbers shown. A cell is a supercell when its number is greater than each immediate neighbour.

One or more options may be correct. Which two claims correctly identify supercells in this row?

options.text: The middle cell $8$ is a supercell, because $8$ is greater than $3$ and greater than $5$.
The left cell $3$ is a supercell, because $3$ is the intended leftmost number.
The right cell $5$ is not a supercell, because $5$ is smaller than its neighbour $8$.
Calling a cell a supercell is what makes its neighbours smaller.

teacher.key_rationale: Middle 8 beats both neighbours, so it is a supercell; right 5 loses to 8, so it is not. Treating the left cell as a supercell because it is leftmost swaps the rule for a label. Saying the supercell label creates smaller neighbours reverses the relation.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source kite-on-grid as a three-cell row filled 3, 8, 5.
